faq.a: The Jupyter Foundation is a directed fund of The Linux Foundation, launched in November 2024, that provides resources for the benefit of Project Jupyter so the project can continue to grow and evolve in the era of AI and collaborative cloud infrastructure. It gives organizations a mechanism to provide sustaining engineering and funding to the project in a vendor-neutral way.

faq.q: How is the Jupyter Foundation different from Project Jupyter?
faq.a: Project Jupyter is the open source project that builds the software and standards; it is developed in the open on GitHub and governed by its own Executive Council and Software Steering Council. The Jupyter Foundation funds and supports that project but does not govern its technical decisions.

Project Jupyter is a non-profit, 100% open source project, born out of IPython in 2014, that creates free software, open standards and web services for interactive computing across all programming languages. Its software and standards are used by millions for interactive computing, data science and research.

faq.q: Which projects and standards are part of Jupyter?
faq.a: Subprojects include JupyterLab, Jupyter Notebook, JupyterHub, Binder, Jupyter Book, Voila and Jupyter Widgets. The open standards are the notebook document format, the interactive computing protocol and the kernel model, which supports over 40 programming languages.

Jupyter and the Jupyter logos are registered trademarks of LF Charities, which hosts Project Jupyter. Referring to Jupyter with the unmodified name or logo is generally allowed; commercial use in product or company names and any modified logo require approval from the Jupyter Trademarks Committee.

The Foundation launched with AWS, Google, Meta and Bloomberg as Premier members, Anaconda, Quansight and QuantStack as General members and MD Anderson Cancer Center as Associate member. The members page now lists Premier members including Apple, Snowflake and Uber, General members including Databricks, JetBrains and Posit, and Associate members including CERN, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory and Columbia University.

about.headline: About Jupyter Foundation
about.intro: The Jupyter Foundation is a directed fund of The Linux Foundation that provides resources to Project Jupyter, so the project can continue to grow and evolve in the era of AI. Project Jupyter's 100% open source software and standards for interactive computing are used by millions and support over 40 programming languages. Launched in November 2024 with founding members including AWS, Google, Meta and Bloomberg, the Foundation is governed by a board of member representatives and Project Jupyter's Executive Council, and funds work in security, accessibility, release management, documentation, community proposals and events. Learn more at jupyterfoundation.org.

sections.title: Our mission
sections.text: The Jupyter Foundation's mission is to provide resources for the benefit of Project Jupyter, so that Project Jupyter may continue to grow and evolve in this era of AI and pervasive, collaborative cloud infrastructure.

sections.title: Our vision
sections.text: A world where everyone can explore data, build knowledge and teach with open tools and open standards for interactive computing.

sections.title: Why now
sections.text: Project Jupyter has become critical infrastructure for data science, AI and education, but a volunteer-led project cannot carry security, release management, accessibility and documentation at that scale on its own. The Foundation adds a mechanism for the organizations that depend on Jupyter to sustain it.

sections.title: Open governance
sections.text: Jupyter Foundation is hosted by the Linux Foundation under a vendor-neutral governance model. A Governing Board oversees budget and strategy; a Technical Committee guides the technical direction.

attrs: Say what the Foundation does in one sentence with the site's own words: provides resources so Project Jupyter can keep growing; no hype adjectives stand in for evidence.
Lead with a sourced number or name (over 40 languages, used by millions, seven funded proposals in 2025, AWS, Google, Meta, Bloomberg) rather than a claim about scale.
Always separate the Foundation (funding and support) from Project Jupyter (technical governance); say vendor-neutral and never imply members steer the roadmap.
Write for researchers, educators and contributors as well as companies; an invitation to join, submit a proposal or attend, in the open, inclusive tone of the Jupyter community.
say: directed fund of The Linux Foundation
avoid: the Jupyter Foundation governs Jupyter's technical direction
the Foundation provides resources; Project Jupyter's Executive Council and Software Steering Council govern the technology
Jupyter is a registered trademark of LF Charities; the Foundation is a directed fund of The Linux Foundation
Jupyter as a verb ("Jupyter your data")
use Jupyter, or Jupyter notebooks, as a noun
JupyterLab, Hub, Book and Notebook as separate products
join the Foundation as a member
